impact.affected_asset: User email and unhidden password displayed in the ExpressVPN Keys autosave iframe.
impact.attacker_capability: After inducing import of a crafted credential record and a later login/autosave display, an attacker can inject CSS into rendered autosave headers and observe requests conditionally triggered by selected credential characters.
impact.security_effect: CSS injection in the extension autosave UI with report-demonstrated CSS-based character-request leakage potential.

causal_trace.summary: A malicious password-import service supplies attacker-controlled credential name or title metadata through an imported CSV record.
Autosave derives header text by substituting existingEntry.title into localized strings and passes it to header components, despite the title being external imported metadata.

BaseHeader renders the supplied text through Vue v-html; UpdateExistingEntry has an alternative v-html header sink from the same existingEntry.title source, with no prior sanitization described by the report.

When a user later logs in and the autosave iframe is shown, injected CSS can cause external requests that encode selected displayed-input characters; the report states the user's email and unhidden password are susceptible to leakage.

failure.operation: Vue v-html rendering of autosave header text derived from existingEntry.title

primary_invariant.statement: Imported credential names and titles must remain non-executable presentation text when rendered in extension autosave UI headers.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The imported title reaches Vue v-html sinks through autosave header construction without prior sanitization, permitting markup containing CSS to be interpreted in the extension UI.

raw_refs.role: canonical audit report with finding narrative, embedded code excerpts, PoC, and remediation status

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report embeds source-to-sink excerpts, a CSV/CSS PoC, mitigation guidance, and states that Cure53 reviewed a vendor diff/PR and verified the issue no longer exists. The reviewed diff/PR, buildable affected source revision, and an execution transcript are not present in this bundle. The PoC and report support CSS-based leakage potential only; this record does not infer arbitrary script execution or a confirmed independent runtime result.

remediation.invariant_restored: Imported title/name values are sanitized or encoded before reaching v-html, so externally supplied credential metadata cannot introduce CSS markup into autosave headers.
mitigation_classes: sanitize imported credential title/name before HTML rendering
HTML-encode imported credential title/name before Vue v-html rendering
